Full blog post on our platform can be found here:

teslascope.com/blog/6.3

It's been a productive week, and we're pleased to announce the release of Teslascope V6.3!

As X is discontinuing Communities (per @nikitabier), we'll share major updates to our platform here from time to time.

1️⃣ We launched early access for our iOS app, via @vehiclescope! 🎉 (invite details in the following post)

2️⃣ You can now sign in with your Apple Account by associating your Apple ID via Account > Integrations. This will also be used to send out invites to our Plus and Pro subscribers in the following weeks.

3️⃣ You can now subscribe without an attached payment method, as long as you have enough credit for the subscription. Subscriptions will automatically pause if there's not enough credit for the renewal.

4️⃣ Added a Vehicle Activity Developer API (combines drives and charges, with more events coming soon!)

5️⃣ Certain vehicle statuses (such as lock status) now update within seconds.

6️⃣ Improved Vehicle Controls to be more performant and reduce wait times.

7️⃣ Improved support for vehicles with special characters and letter modifiers.

Additional improvements are underway for the remainder of May.

We noticed a new Tesla software update 2026.8.200 (factory update) on a Tesla vehicle (2026). View the rollout of this update here: teslascope.com/software/2026…

Factory updates are available to recently delivered vehicles only.

Our own HW3 vehicle (a 2018 Model 3 Performance) is also included in this initial wave.

We've received several reports that this download was initiated over cellular, suggesting it contains critical security fixes. AI4 vehicles on 2026.2.9.10 will receive these fixes very soon.

2026.14.6 is going out en masse to HW3 and AI4 vehicles, which contains security improvements (in addition to the Spring Update features from 2026.14.3).

Here's a breakdown of the specific models receiving the update, along with the release notes.

Usage of FSD V14.3.2 is looking great on 2026.2.9.10:

37.5% of drivers use FSD, and it is activated for an average of 88.8% of each drive.

In 2026.2.9.1 (V14.2.2.5), FSD was used by 22.2% of drivers, at 86.6% self-driven.

A 0.7x increase in utilization is a fantastic sign.
